body:
Closes #37.

A visit can now record the vet who attended it, and the vet is optional. You can pick a vet when booking or editing a visit, or leave it empty, since the vet is often unknown when the appointment is made. The owner's page, the all-visits screen and the chatbot's visit list now show each visit's vet. A visit without one reads "No vet"; that includes every visit created before this change. The data model is a nullable `visits.vet_id` (migration V4). The API adds `vetId` plus read-only vet first and last names to the visit payloads. A few demo seed visits get a vet so both states show up.

Two decisions deserve a reviewer's eye. First, editing a visit (PUT) replaces it whole, so a request without `vetId` clears the vet. That is what makes clearing the field persist, as the ticket requires, but a client that omits the field will also wipe the vet. Second, deleting a vet keeps their visits and sets the vet to none (`ON DELETE SET NULL`); refusing the delete would also be defensible. Still open: an unknown `vetId` returns 404, the same as an unknown pet type, rather than 400. The chatbot's `create_visit` can't choose a vet. The new Angular specs have only run in CI, since npm couldn't run in my session. Separately, this branch's CI cancels itself: the push and pull-request runs share one concurrency group, so CI on the fix commit only went green after a manual re-run. That workflow fix belongs on `main`.

<!-- hr:merge-risk -->
**Merge risk**
- Two-way door: ✅ a nullable vet column that a revert simply stops using; but a PUT that omits vetId clears the vet
- Blast radius: ◔ **visits API** (about a quarter of the system)
<!-- /hr:merge-risk -->
